correctness.rationale: A centered Euclidean point configuration has unit squared length on every graph edge and variance V. The Rayleigh trace identity gives the global upper bound λ2≤B/V for arbitrary nonnegative conductances. The proposed positive edge weights satisfy LQ=λQ_centered for every coordinate. The invariant anti-symmetric 2x2 and symmetric 3x3 spectral blocks each have exactly one λ positive mode; their other eigenvalue exceeds λ since the pendant edge conductance is strictly greater than λ. Peripheral-difference modes have λ with multiplicity k−1, so λ2=λ with total multiplicity k+1. Unit edge lengths and trace equality imply budget B=λV. Uniqueness of scalar root follows from a strictly decreasing function on (0,1). Direct asymptotics give the stated limit. A separate numerical implementation assembled matrices and checked the formulas for 33 graph sizes; the infinite result uses proof, not the finite list.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General semidefinite or symmetry methods are computational formulations rather than explicit all-size classifications. The lollipop formula is for a different topology and discrete-time SLEM, which has upper spectral and vertex stochastic constraints absent from an unrestricted continuous-time rate budget. No known general theorem was found that implies the proposed explicit scalar algebraic root and weights.

originality.rationale: The exact all-size continuous-time total-budget spectral-gap formula for the two distinct attachment hubs, positive edge rates and Fiedler multiplicity are not implied by the inspected primary results. Sun et al. provide a general SDP and variance dual without this solved graph family; Jafarizadeh treats discrete-time SLEM and different attachment structures. Related explicit problems for a one-tail clique, bridged clique pair and one-leaf biclique have nonisomorphic supports and do not yield the present formula. Searches for analogous results under alternative graph names found no implication-equivalent solution. Specialized prior coverage is still possible.
residual_risks: An earlier exact spectral-design calculation using a different name (e.g. two-whisker clique or a block graph) may have escaped semantic indexing.
The 2009 symmetry paper was assessed only from its arXiv abstract after PDF retrieval failed; its general technique could contain a specialized hidden example.
The 2025 clique-lift work was inspected in relevant open-text sections, not page-by-page in every appendix; present graph differs from the stated clique-lift and lollipop definitions.

value.rationale: A complete family of clique networks with two different pendant bottlenecks is a natural model for allocating a fixed total diffusion/consensus coupling budget. An explicit all-size rate allocation, algebraic root, global upper-bound certificate, Fiedler multiplicity, and asymptotic optimum answer a concrete network design question that generic SDP solvability does not quantify. The precision matters for implementing sparse attachments and benchmarking high-multiplicity semidefinite optima; it is not a renaming of the single-tail graph or a fixed tiny-graph enumeration.
